text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Zambia Federation of Employers has urged government to start salary negotiations with workers before next year's Budget is drawn up to avoid a crisis.
- Government will punish a cleaning company that dumped human excreta near a stream in Lusaka causing a cholera outbreak that claimed one life, environment minister William Harrington said.
- Former foreign affairs minister Vernon Mwaanga has sued American magazine, Newsweek, for libel and is demanding $50,000 in damages and a retraction on a story linking him to drug trafficking.

- President Frederick Chiluba on Monday commended mining house Anglovaal Ltd for starting exploratory work at Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) Konkola North even before an agreement was signed.
- The family of former legal affairs minister Luminzu Shimaponda, who died in a South African hospital last week, claims he was poisoned.

- A group of opposition parties on Monday filed an injunction restraining the electoral commission from holding local government elections using the current voters register, which omits half of the country's 4.6 potential voters.
